q: A can complete a work in 14 days. What part of the work does A complete in one day?
exp: If the complete work takes 14 days, one day's work is 1/14 of the total work.

q: A can complete a work in 16 days. How many days will he need to complete one-fourth of the work?
exp: One-fourth of the work requires one-fourth of the time: 16/4 = 4 days.

q: A can complete a work in 9 days and B can complete it in 18 days. How many days will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/9 + 1/18 = 1/6. Therefore they take 6 days.

q: If 4 workers complete a job in 10 days, how many worker-days are required?
exp: Worker-days = 4 × 10 = 40.

q: A worker earns ₹750 for 5 days. What is his daily wage?
exp: Daily wage = ₹750/5 = ₹150.

q: A can do a work in 12 days and B can do the same work in 24 days. Who is more efficient?
exp: A takes less time, so A has the higher efficiency.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 5 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill in one hour?
exp: The pipe fills 1/5 of the tank in one hour.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours. How long does it take to fill half the tank?
exp: Half the tank requires half the filling time: 10/2 = 5 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours and another pipe fills it in 12 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/12 = 1/6. Time = 6 hours.

q: A can complete a work in 8 days. B is twice as efficient as A. How many days will B take?
exp: Twice the efficiency means half the time. B takes 8/2 = 4 days.

q: A completes 1/6 of a work in one day. How many days are needed for the whole work?
exp: If one day's work is 1/6, the complete work requires 6 days.

q: If 6 workers earn ₹3,600 equally for a day's work, what is each worker's wage?
exp: Each worker receives ₹3,600/6 = ₹600.

q: A can complete a work in 20 days. How much work does he complete in 10 days?
exp: Work completed = 10/20 = 1/2.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and another pipe fills it in 16 hours. How much of the tank do they fill together in one hour?
exp: Combined work = 1/8 + 1/16 = 3/16 of the tank per hour.

q: If 10 workers complete a job in 6 days, how many days will 5 workers take, assuming equal efficiency?
exp: Total work = 10×6 = 60 worker-days. Five workers need 60/5 = 12 days.

q: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 15 days. How many days will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/15 = 3/20. Time = 20/3 = 6⅔ days.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days and B in 27 days. How much of the work will they complete together in 6 days?
exp: Combined rate = 1/18 + 1/27 = 5/54. In 6 days they complete 30/54 = 5/9.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 10 days. A alone can complete it in 15 days. How many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. Therefore B takes 30 days.

q: A can complete a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. A works for 5 days and then B completes the remaining work. How many days does B need?
exp: A completes 5/20 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. B's rate is 1/30, so time = 3/4×30 = 22.5 days.

q: A is 25% more efficient than B. If B takes 20 days to complete a work, how many days will A take?
exp: A's efficiency is 1.25 times B's. A's time = 20/1.25 = 16 days.

q: A is 50% more efficient than B. If A takes 12 days, how many days will B take?
exp: A's efficiency is 1.5 times B's, so B's time = 12×1.5 = 18 days.

q: A can do a work in 24 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. How many days will they take together?
exp: B takes 24/1.5 = 16 days. Combined rate = 1/24 + 1/16 = 5/48, so time = 48/5 = 9.6 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. B alone takes 24 days. How many days will A alone take?
exp: A's rate = 1/8 − 1/24 = 1/12. Therefore A takes 12 days.

q: A can complete a work in 16 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 4 days. What fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/16 + 1/24 = 5/48. Four days complete 5/12, leaving 7/12.

q: A can complete a work in 30 days and B in 20 days. If they work together for 6 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/30 + 1/20 = 1/12. Six days complete 1/2, so 1/2 remains.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours and another fills it in 8 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/8 = 5/24. Time = 24/5 = 4.8 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 15 hours and a leak empties it in 30 hours. If both are open, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/15 − 1/30 = 1/30. Therefore the tank fills in 30 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and a second pipe empties it in 20 hours. If both are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/10 − 1/20 = 1/20. Therefore the tank fills in 20 hours.

q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 18 minutes respectively. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. Because of a leak, it takes 8 hours to fill. How long would the leak alone take to empty the tank?
exp: Leak rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = 1/24. Hence the leak alone empties the tank in 24 hours.

q: Five workers complete a job in 18 days. How many days will 9 workers take for the same job, assuming equal efficiency?
exp: Total work = 5×18 = 90 worker-days. Nine workers need 90/9 = 10 days.

q: Eight workers complete a work in 15 days. If 2 workers leave after 5 days, how many more days will the remaining workers need?
exp: Total work = 8×15 = 120 worker-days. Work done in 5 days = 40. Remaining = 80. Six workers need 80/6 = 13⅓ days, so none of the options is correct.

q: Six workers complete a job in 20 days. If 4 additional workers join from the beginning, how many days will the job take?
exp: Total work = 6×20 = 120 worker-days. With 10 workers, time = 120/10 = 12 days.

q: A and B receive ₹4,000 for completing a work. A completes 3/8 of the work. What is B's share?
exp: B completes 5/8 of the work. B's share = 5/8×₹4,000 = ₹2,500.

q: Three workers work for 5, 7 and 8 days respectively at the same daily wage. If the total wage is ₹4,000, what is the second worker's share?
exp: Total worker-days = 5+7+8 = 20. Second worker's share = 7/20×4000 = ₹1,400.

q: A can do a work in 25 days and B in 20 days. If A works for 5 days and B works for 4 days, what fraction of the work is completed?
exp: A completes 5/25 = 1/5. B completes 4/20 = 1/5. Total = 2/5, so the correct option is the second.

q: A can complete a work in 15 days. B can complete it in 10 days. If B works alone for 4 days, what fraction of the work remains?
exp: B completes 4/10 = 2/5. Remaining = 3/5.

q: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days will A need?
exp: Together rate = 5/36. In 2 days they complete 5/18. Remaining = 13/18. A's rate is 1/12, so time = 13/18×12 = 26/3 = 8⅔ days. None of the options is exact.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 9 hours and another pipe fills it in 18 hours. How much of the tank is filled in 3 hours when both are open?
exp: Combined rate = 1/9 + 1/18 = 1/6. In 3 hours they fill 3/6 = 1/2.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 20 minutes and another in 30 minutes. If both are opened for 8 minutes, what fraction of the tank is filled?
exp: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12. In 8 minutes, 8/12 = 2/3, so none of the options is correct.

q: A worker completes 40% of a job in 8 days. At the same rate, how many days are required for the whole job?
exp: If 40% takes 8 days, 100% takes 8/0.4 = 20 days.

q: A and B together complete a work in 12 days. A alone takes 20 days. How many days will B alone take?
exp: B's rate = 1/12 − 1/20 = 1/30. Therefore B takes 30 days.

q: A can complete a work in 40 days and B in 60 days. They work together for 12 days. What fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/40 + 1/60 = 1/24. In 12 days they complete 1/2, so 1/2 remains. The correct option is the second.

q: A can complete a work in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work together for 3 days and then A leaves. How many more days will B need?
exp: Together rate = 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6. In 3 days they complete 1/2. Remaining = 1/2. B needs 15/2 = 7.5 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 6 days. A is twice as efficient as B. How many days will B alone take?
exp: Let B's rate be x and A's rate 2x. Then 3x = 1/6, so x = 1/18. B takes 18 days.

q: A is 20% more efficient than B. If B completes a work in 24 days, how many days will A take?
exp: A's efficiency is 1.2 times B's. A's time = 24/1.2 = 20 days.

q: A can complete a work in 30 days and B in 45 days. They work together for 9 days. What fraction of the work remains?
exp: Combined rate = 1/30 + 1/45 = 1/18. In 9 days they complete 1/2, so 1/2 remains. The correct option is the third.

q: A, B and C can complete a work alone in 12, 18 and 36 days respectively. They work together for 3 days, after which C leaves. How many more days will A and B need?
exp: Combined rate of A, B and C = 1/12+1/18+1/36 = 1/6. In 3 days they complete 1/2. A+B rate = 5/36. Remaining half takes (1/2)×36/5 = 3.6 days.

q: A and B together can complete a work in 10 days. A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days will A alone take?
exp: Let B's rate be x. A's rate is 1.5x, so together 2.5x = 1/10. A's rate = 1/25? Specifically x=1/25, so A=3/50 and A's time = 50/3 = 16⅔ days.

q: A, B and C can complete a work in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. A and B work for 5 days, then C joins them. How many total days are needed?
exp: A+B rate = 1/20+1/30 = 1/12. In 5 days they complete 5/12. Remaining = 7/12. All three rate = 1/10, so remaining time = 35/6 = 5⅚ days. Total = 10⅚ days, so none of the options is exact.

q: A can complete a work in 24 days. B is twice as efficient as A and C is half as efficient as A. How many days will all three take together?
exp: Rates relative to A are 1, 2 and 1/2. Total rate = 3.5/24 = 7/48. Time = 48/7 = 6 6/7 days, so none of the options is exact.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours, B in 18 hours, and a leak empties it in 36 hours. If all are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/18 − 1/36 = 1/9. Therefore the tank fills in 9 hours.

q: Two pipes fill a tank in 15 and 20 minutes respectively, while a third pipe empties it in 60 minutes. How long will the tank take to fill when all are open?
exp: Net rate = 1/15 + 1/20 − 1/60 = 1/10. Therefore the tank fills in 10 minutes.

q: A and B can complete a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. How many days will all three take together?
exp: Adding the three pair rates gives 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 1/5. This equals twice the combined rate of A, B and C. Hence their combined rate is 1/10 and they take 10 days.

q: A can complete a work in 18 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 6 days, after which B leaves. How many more days will A need?
exp: Together rate = 1/18+1/24 = 7/72. In 6 days they complete 7/12. Remaining = 5/12. A takes (5/12)×18 = 7.5 days, so none of the options is exact.

q: Eight workers can complete a work in 15 days. After 5 days, three workers leave. How many more days will the remaining workers need?
exp: Total work = 8×15 = 120 worker-days. Work done in 5 days = 40. Remaining = 80. Five workers need 80/5 = 16 days, so none of the options is correct.

q: A worker is 25% more efficient than another worker. If together they complete a work in 18 days, how many days would the less efficient worker take alone?
exp: Let the less efficient worker's rate be x. The other rate is 1.25x. Together 2.25x = 1/18, so x = 1/40.5. Thus the less efficient worker takes 40.5 days, so the second option is correct.
